Correct names in bipartite interaction matrix


```{r}
# Create a named vector mapping species codes to species names
species_mapping <- species_names_df %>%
  dplyr::select(species, species_name) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  deframe()  # Convert to a named vector for direct mapping

# Replace rownames in bipartite_matrix using species_mapping
rownames(bipartite_matrix) <- species_mapping[rownames(bipartite_matrix)]

# Check for any NA values in row names (i.e., species not found in mapping)
if (any(is.na(rownames(bipartite_matrix)))) {
  cat("Warning: Some species codes were not found in species_names_df:\n")
  print(rownames(bipartite_matrix)[is.na(rownames(bipartite_matrix))])
}

# Modify row names of bipartite_matrix
rownames(bipartite_matrix) <- rownames(bipartite_matrix) %>%
  gsub("\\.", "", .) %>%  # Remove periods
  gsub("_", "", .) %>% 
  gsub(" ", "", .)        # Remove spaces

# Verify the updated row names
print(rownames(bipartite_matrix))

```

```{r}
# Step 1: Merge the two datasets by 'naesiotus_sp'
merged_data <- aggregated_otu_data %>%
  left_join(otu_metadata %>% dplyr::select(naesiotus_sp, island), by = "naesiotus_sp")

# Step 1.1: Aggregate the OTU data per snail species
merged_data_persnail <- merged_data %>%
  rename(species_name = naesiotus_sp) |> 
  group_by(species_name, island) %>%  # Group by both snail species and island
  summarise(across(starts_with("OTU"), sum, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # Sum the OTU columns
  ungroup()


# Step 2: Function to create a bipartite network for each island
create_bipartite_network <- function(island_name, data) {
  # Filter for the specific island
  island_data <- data %>% filter(island == !!island_name)
  
  # Reshape the data to long format to create the edges between snails and OTUs
  edges <- island_data %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("OTU"), names_to = "OTU", values_to = "count") %>%
    filter(count > 0) %>%
    dplyr::select(species_name, OTU) %>%
    mutate(island = island_name)  # Assign island to edges
  
  # Create a bipartite graph
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE)
  
  # Get the number of species (snails) and OTUs
  num_species <- length(unique(edges$species_name))
  num_otus <- length(unique(edges$OTU))
  
  # Assign bipartite types (TRUE for species, FALSE for OTUs)
  V(g)$type <- c(rep(TRUE, num_species), rep(FALSE, num_otus))
  
  V(g)$island <- island_name # Add island as a node trait
  
  # Assign island attribute to edges
  E(g)$island <- edges$island

  return(g)
}

# Step 3: Function to plot the network with island-colored links
# Step 3: Function to plot the network with island-colored links
plot_custom_bipartite_network <- function(g, island_name) {
  ggraph(g, layout = "bipartite") +
    
    # Color edges based on island
    geom_edge_link(aes(color = island), edge_alpha = 0.8, edge_width = 0.6) +
    scale_edge_color_manual(values = island_colors, name = "Island") +  # Use island colors
    
    # Customize nodes: All in grey30
    geom_node_point(aes(shape = factor(V(g)$type)), 
                    size = 5, stroke = 1, alpha = 0.7, fill = "grey30", color = "grey30") +
    
    # Show shape legend only
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), labels = c("Nematode OTUs", "Naesiotus sp")) +
    
    labs(shape = "Guild") +  # Only show shape legend
    
    ggtitle(island_name) +  # Add the island name as a title
    
    theme_void() +  # Clean background with no axes or gridlines
    theme(legend.position = "right",  # Adjust legend position
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  # Center the title
}


# Step 4: Create and plot bipartite networks for all islands
islands <- unique(merged_data_persnail$island)
plots <- list()

#saveRDS(islands,here::here("output/temporal_output/islands.rds"))

for (island in islands) {
  g <- create_bipartite_network(island, merged_data_persnail)
  p <- plot_custom_bipartite_network(g, island)
  plots[[island]] <- p
}

# Step 5: Arrange the plots in a grid using ggarrange
ggarrange(plotlist = plots, ncol = 2, nrow = ceiling(length(plots)/2),
          common.legend = TRUE, legend = "top")


ggsave(here::here("output/figures/islandnetworks_bipartiteplot2.png"), height = 12, width = 8)
```

```{r}
# List of extinct species
extinct_species <- c("cavagnaroi", "eschariferus", "lycodus", "olla", "planospira")

# Species not in the phylogeny
missing_in_phylogeny <- c("pinzonopsis")


plot_custom_bipartite_network <- function(g, island_name) {
  
  # Extract node names
  node_names <- V(g)$name
  
  # Assign default fill color (OTUs = grey70, Snails = grey30)
  node_fill <- rep("grey70", length(node_names))  # Default OTU color
  node_fill[V(g)$type] <- "grey30"  # Change Snails to grey30
  
  # Assign extinct species as black
  node_fill[node_names %in% extinct_species] <- "black"
  
  # Assign missing species in phylogeny as white
  node_fill[node_names %in% missing_in_phylogeny] <- "white"
  
  # Assign border color (only for missing species in phylogeny)
  border_color <- rep("black", length(node_names))  # Default black border
  border_color[node_names %in% missing_in_phylogeny] <- "black"  # Black border for missing species
  
  # Assign shape types (Snails vs. OTUs)
  shape_type <- ifelse(V(g)$type, "Snail", "OTU")  # Shape mapping
  
  # Store attributes in the graph
  V(g)$node_fill <- node_fill
  V(g)$border_color <- border_color
  V(g)$shape_type <- shape_type  # Store shape types for ggplot
  
  # **Ensure there are no missing values in node attributes**
  node_data <- data.frame(
    Name = node_names,
    Type = shape_type,
    Fill = node_fill,
    Border = border_color
  )
  
  # Remove any nodes with NA fill (debugging)
  node_data <- node_data %>% drop_na(Fill)
  
  print(node_data)  # Check node attributes before plotting
  
  # Ensure edges don't have missing values
  if (length(E(g)) == 0) {
    cat("Warning: No edges present in the graph for island:", island_name, "\n")
    return(NULL)  # Skip empty graphs
  }
  
  # **Create the plot**
  p <- ggraph(g, layout = "bipartite") +
    
    # Color edges based on island
    geom_edge_link(aes(color = island), edge_alpha = 0.8, edge_width = 0.6) +
    scale_edge_color_manual(values = island_colors, name = "Island") +  # Use island colors
    
    # Customize nodes
    geom_node_point(aes(shape = shape_type, fill = node_fill, color = border_color), 
                    size = 5, stroke = 1.2, alpha = 1.0, na.rm = TRUE) +  
    
    # **Fix color mapping**
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey30" = "grey30", "black" = "black", "white" = "white")) +  
    scale_color_manual(values = c("black" = "black")) +  
    
    # Customize node shapes: 16 = circle (OTUs), 17 = triangle (Snails)
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("OTU" = 16, "Snail" = 17), labels = c("Nematode OTUs", "Naesiotus sp")) +
    
    labs(shape = "Guild") +  # Only show shape legend
    
    ggtitle(island_name) +  # Add the island name as a title
    
    theme_void() +  # Clean background with no axes or gridlines
    theme(legend.position = "right",  # Adjust legend position
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  # Center the title
  
  return(p)
}

plot_custom_bipartite_network <- function(g, island_name) {
  
  # Extract node names
  node_names <- V(g)$name
  
  # Assign default colors (Snails = grey30, OTUs = grey70)
  node_fill <- ifelse(V(g)$type, "grey30", "grey70")  
  border_color <- rep(NA, length(node_names))  # Default: No border
  
  # Assign extinct species as black
  node_fill[node_names %in% extinct_species] <- "black"
  
  # Assign missing species in phylogeny as white with black border
  node_fill[node_names %in% missing_in_phylogeny] <- "white"
  border_color[node_names %in% missing_in_phylogeny] <- "black"  # Black border
  
  # Assign shape types (Snails = 17, OTUs = 16)
  shape_type <- ifelse(V(g)$type, "Snail", "OTU")  

  # Store attributes in the graph object
  V(g)$node_fill <- node_fill
  V(g)$border_color <- border_color
  V(g)$shape_type <- shape_type  

  # Convert node attributes to a dataframe for debugging
  node_data <- data.frame(
    Name = node_names,
    Type = shape_type,
    Fill = node_fill,
    Border = border_color
  )
  
  print(node_data)  # Debugging: Ensure correct node attributes before plotting
  
  # **Handle cases where there are no edges**
  if (length(E(g)) == 0) {
    cat("⚠️ Warning: No edges present in the graph for island:", island_name, "\n")
    return(NULL)  # Skip empty graphs
  }
  
  # **Create the plot**
  p <- ggraph(g, layout = "bipartite") +
    
    # Color edges based on island
    geom_edge_link(aes(color = island), edge_alpha = 0.8, edge_width = 0.6) +
    scale_edge_color_manual(values = island_colors, name = "Island") +  
    
    # Customize nodes
    geom_node_point(aes(shape = shape_type, fill = node_fill, color = border_color), 
                    size = 5, stroke = 1.2, alpha = 1.0, na.rm = TRUE) +  
    
    # Ensure colors are correctly mapped
    scale_fill_identity() +  # Use the manually assigned fill colors
    scale_color_identity() +  # Use manually assigned border colors
    
    # Customize node shapes: 16 = circle (OTUs), 17 = triangle (Snails)
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("OTU" = 16, "Snail" = 17), labels = c("Nematode OTUs", "Naesiotus sp")) +
    
    labs(shape = "Guild") +  # Only show shape legend
    
    ggtitle(island_name) +  # Add the island name as a title
    
    theme_void() +  # Clean background with no axes or gridlines
    theme(legend.position = "right",  
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  

  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
# List of extinct species
# Define the target island
# Define the target island
island_name <- "Fernandina"

# Step 1: Filter the data for the island
island_data <- merged_data_persnail %>% filter(island == island_name)
print(paste("Processing island:", island_name))  # Debugging print statement

# Step 2: Reshape data to long format to create edges
edges <- island_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("OTU"), names_to = "OTU", values_to = "count") %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(species_name, OTU) %>%
  mutate(island = island_name)

print(edges)  # Debugging: Check edges

# Step 3: Create a bipartite graph
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE)

# Step 4: Assign node types
V(g)$type <- ifelse(V(g)$name %in% edges$species_name, TRUE, FALSE)

# Step 5: Assign colors (ALL grey30)
V(g)$node_fill <- "grey30"  # Fill = grey30
V(g)$border_color <- "grey30"  # Border = grey30

# Step 6: Create a custom layout to **reduce separation**
layout_custom <- create_layout(g, layout = "bipartite")
layout_custom$y <- ifelse(V(g)$type, 0, 0.5)  # Reduce separation (was 0 and 1)

# Step 7: Generate the plot
p <- ggraph(layout_custom) +
  
  # Color edges based on island
  geom_edge_link(aes(color = factor(island)), edge_alpha = 0.6, edge_width = 0.6) +
  scale_edge_color_manual(values = island_colors, name = "Island") +  
  
  # Ensure nodes are plotted with correct fill, border, and transparency
  geom_node_point(aes(shape = factor(V(g)$type)),  
                  fill = "grey30",  # All nodes filled with grey30
                  color = "grey30",  # Border also grey30
                  size = 5, stroke = 1.2, alpha = 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) +  

  # Add labels only for Naesiotus species (Snail nodes)

  # Customize node shapes: 16 = circle (OTUs), 17 = triangle (Snails)
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 17), labels = c("Nematode OTUs", "Naesiotus sp")) +

  labs(shape = "Guild") +  # Only show shape legend

  ggtitle(island_name) +  # Add the island name as a title

  theme_void() +  # Clean background with no axes or gridlines
  theme(legend.position = "right",  
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  

# Step 8: Print plot
print(p)



ggsave(here::here("output/figures/fernandina.png"), height = 2, width = 3)
```

```{r}
df_island <- read_excel(path = here::here("data/19july24_datalab.xlsx"), sheet = "island_characteristics")

df_island$min_emergence <- as.numeric(df_island$min_emergence)
df_island$max_emergence <- as.numeric(df_island$max_emergence)

# Calculate the mean difference between min_emergence and max_emergence
mean_diff <- df_island %>%
  filter(!is.na(min_emergence) & !is.na(max_emergence)) %>%
  mutate(diff = max_emergence - min_emergence) %>%
  summarise(mean_diff = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(mean_diff)

# Estimate max_emergence for Champion by adding the mean difference to its min_emergence
df_island <- df_island %>%
  mutate(max_emergence = ifelse(is.na(max_emergence), min_emergence + mean_diff, max_emergence))

# Rename the column "mean_emergence" to "island_age" in df_island
# add an ID column
df_island <- df_island %>% dplyr::rename(island_area = area) |> 
  mutate(island_code = as.numeric(as.factor(island)))


# increase max. emergence of Sants Fe by a small amount - min. and max for this island are the same and this gives error in the model when trying to estimate the approximate age.

df_island <- df_island |> 
  dplyr::mutate(max_emergence = ifelse(island == "Santa_Fe", max_emergence + 0.1, max_emergence))


df_island
```

```{r}
# Merge Gardner with Espanola
otu_metadata <- otu_metadata %>%
  mutate(island = ifelse(island == "Gardner", "Espanola", island))

# Filter islands with at least two snail species
valid_islands <- otu_metadata %>%
  group_by(island) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(naesiotus_sp) >= 2) %>%
  pull(island) %>%
  unique()

# Prepare data frame to store results
network_statistics <- data.frame()

# Loop through each valid island
for (island in valid_islands) {
  print(paste("Processing island:", island))
  
  # Filter metadata for the current island
  island_metadata <- otu_metadata %>% filter(island == !!island)
  
  # Get snail species for the island
  island_snails <- unique(island_metadata$naesiotus_sp)
  
  # Subset bipartite matrix
  island_matrix <- bipartite_matrix[rownames(bipartite_matrix) %in% island_snails, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Skip invalid matrices
  if (nrow(island_matrix) == 0 || ncol(island_matrix) == 0 || 
      all(rowSums(island_matrix) == 0) || all(colSums(island_matrix) == 0)) {
    message("Skipping island due to invalid matrix: ", island)
    next
  }
  
  # Create graph
  g <- graph_from_biadjacency_matrix(island_matrix, directed = FALSE)
  
  # Compute modularity
  compute_modularity <- function(g) {
    mod_louvain <- cluster_louvain(g)$modularity
    mod_walktrap <- modularity(cluster_walktrap(g))
    mod_fast_greedy <- modularity(cluster_fast_greedy(g))
    mod_leading_eigen <- cluster_leading_eigen(g)$modularity
    mean_modularity <- mean(c(mod_louvain, mod_walktrap, mod_fast_greedy, mod_leading_eigen), na.rm = TRUE)
    return(mean_modularity)
  }
  modularity <- compute_modularity(g)
  
  # Compute nestedness
  nestedness <- nestednodf(island_matrix)$statistic["NODF"]
  
  # Compute H2 specialization
  H2_specialization <- H2fun(island_matrix)
  
  # Compute mean and SD specialization (d) for snails and OTUs
  snail_d <- dfun(island_matrix)$dprime
  otu_d <- dfun(t(island_matrix))$dprime
  
  mean_snail_d <- mean(snail_d, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_snail_d <- sd(snail_d, na.rm = TRUE)
  mean_otu_d <- mean(otu_d, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_otu_d <- sd(otu_d, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Append results to data frame
  network_statistics <- rbind(network_statistics, data.frame(
    island = island,
    modularity = modularity,
    nestedness = nestedness,
    H2 = H2_specialization,
    mean_snail_d = mean_snail_d,
    sd_snail_d = sd_snail_d,
    mean_otu_d = mean_otu_d,
    sd_otu_d = sd_otu_d
  ))
}

# Add island age and area to the statistics
df_island <- df_island %>%
  mutate(mean_age = (min_emergence + max_emergence) / 2)

network_statistics <- network_statistics %>%
  left_join(df_island %>% dplyr::select(island, mean_age, island_area), by = "island")

network_statistics
```

distribution of specialization per island

```{r}

# Prepare data frame to store individual d' values
specialization_data <- data.frame()

# Loop through each valid island
for (island in valid_islands) {
  print(paste("Processing island:", island))
  
  # Filter metadata for the current island
  island_metadata <- otu_metadata %>% filter(island == !!island)
  
  # Get snail species for the island
  island_snails <- unique(island_metadata$naesiotus_sp)
  
  # Subset bipartite matrix
  island_matrix <- bipartite_matrix[rownames(bipartite_matrix) %in% island_snails, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Skip invalid matrices
  if (nrow(island_matrix) == 0 || ncol(island_matrix) == 0 || 
      all(rowSums(island_matrix) == 0) || all(colSums(island_matrix) == 0)) {
    message("Skipping island due to invalid matrix: ", island)
    next
  }
  
  # Compute specialization (d')
  snail_d <- dfun(island_matrix)$dprime
  otu_d <- dfun(t(island_matrix))$dprime
  
  # Store individual d' values
  snail_data <- data.frame(island = island, species = names(snail_d), specialization = snail_d, group = "Snails")
  otu_data <- data.frame(island = island, species = names(otu_d), specialization = otu_d, group = "OTUs")
  
  # Merge snail and OTU data
  specialization_data <- rbind(specialization_data, snail_data, otu_data)
}

# Convert island to factor for ordered plotting
specialization_data$island <- factor(specialization_data$island, levels = unique(specialization_data$island))

# Ensure network_statistics has only unique islands
network_statistics_unique <- network_statistics %>%
  distinct(island, .keep_all = TRUE)  # Keeps only one row per island

# Now join without duplication issues
specialization_data <- specialization_data %>%
  left_join(network_statistics_unique %>% 
              dplyr::select(island, mean_age, island_area, log_island_area), 
            by = "island")



# 🎨 **Plot the Distribution**
plot_specialization_distribution <- ggplot(specialization_data, aes(x = factor(log_island_area), y = specialization, fill = group)) +
  
  # Boxplot
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +  

  # Jitter points for visualization (fixing the error)
  geom_jitter(aes(color = group), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +  

  # Colors for Snails and OTUs
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Snails" = "#009E73", "OTUs" = "#E69F00")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Snails" = "#009E73", "OTUs" = "#E69F00")) +  

  # Labels and Theme
  labs(x = "Island (log Area)", y = "Specialization (d')", fill = "Group") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate labels

# Print the plot
print(plot_specialization_distribution)



```
